newsitem.title: USA: IMF's Camdessus sees scope Italy rate cuts--Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus sees scope Italy rate cuts--Ciampi.

text.p: IMF managing director Michel Camdessus sees scope for further interest rate cuts in Italy if the government continues on its current path of fiscal correction, Italy's Treasury and Budget Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Saturday.
"If Italy continues its policy of reducing the public deficit there will be room for further cuts in (Italian) interest rates," Ciampi told a press conference.
"Italian interest rates could fall even if Germany does not lower its rates and perhaps even if it raises them, Camdessus said," said Ciampi, who met with Camdessus earlier.
Ciampi explained that that was because "the differential between Italian and German interest rates is so wide that just by improving inflation Italian rates would have scope to fall."

Ciampi also said that in his meeting with the International Monetary Fund's Camdessus, "We confirmed clearly that Italy is pursuing a path toward stability with its fiscal policy, to the benefit not only of public finances, but of the entire economy."
Ciampi also confirmed his government's intention to bring the lira back into Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism.
He added that the task was made easier by the 60 trillion lira budget package the government approved Friday.
The lira's re-entry "has been and is in Italy's intentions. It will be made easier by the passage (of the budget plan)," Ciampi said.
